clue.text: Midshipman (the one wearing a medal) relaxed

parts.note: Mr Midshipman Easy is the title hero of Captain Marryat's naval novel

indicators.note: the medal word has the one word on it, as if dressed in it, so it goes round

parts.note: a gong is slang for a medal or decoration
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A young naval officer who has won a medal takes things in his stride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' signals the container. The midshipman is the title hero of Captain Marryat's novel Mr Midshipman Easy; 'the' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone easygoing is calm and unworried, a synonym of relaxed.

clue.text: Lengthening next one is different

indicators.note: the letters come out differently arranged

explanation.surface: Each new extra piece added to the length turns out to be unlike the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is different' rearranges NEXT ONE IS; the 'is' does double duty only in the surface, as the letters of 'is' are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension is an added stretch, the act or result of lengthening.

clue.text: Young man joins society with someone sanctimonious

parts.note: a prig is a self-righteous, smug person

explanation.surface: A youth enters a club full of holier-than-thou members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joins' simply links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprig is a dated word for a youth or young fellow, a scion of a family.

clue.text: Dictionary giving 'paint' a line

parts.note: gloss is a shiny paint
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A reference book gives a fresh sheen to a written line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving' just links the definition to the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is a list of words with their meanings, a small specialised dictionary.

clue.text: The game is as good as won

definitions.text: The game is as good as won

parts.words: The game is as good as won
parts.note: read as a hunting phrase: the shot birds are already in the game bag; read as an idiom: victory is certain

explanation.surface: With a match nearly over, success is assured.
explanation.walkthrough: The shooting sense of game, birds killed and bagged, lies behind the everyday idiom for a certainty.
explanation.definitionFit: A result secured or assured is said colloquially to be in the bag, like birds already shot.

clue.text: In class, one displays exceptional ability

indicators.note: the one word goes in the class word

parts.note: a genus is a class in biological classification
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: In every class there is one pupil who shows outstanding talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts I inside GENUS; 'displays' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Genius means extraordinary talent or brilliance.

clue.text: Born, *I'm told, in the Tyrol. I'm Italian

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held and printed as 'Born, I'm told, in the Tyrol. I'm Italian (5)': no reading of these words gives LIMIT and none of them defines it; the clue appears to belong to another entry or puzzle.
annotationWithheld.clue: Born, *I'm told, in the Tyrol. I'm Italian

clue.text: It's clear the devil wears a hat

indicators.note: the hat goes on round the devil, which wears it

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
an imp is a little devil

explanation.surface: Plainly the devil is wearing headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wears' signals the container: a hat goes round its wearer's head. 'It's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid water is transparent, so limpid is a synonym of clear.

clue.text: Not well educated; dim over anything at all

indicators.note: in a down clue the dim word sits over the anything word

parts.note: to mist is to dim or blur, as glass does
aught is an old word for anything whatever

explanation.surface: A dull pupil has no knowledge of anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places MIST above AUGHT in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistaught means wrongly or badly taught, so poorly schooled.

clue.text: Guy in the river, we hear

indicators.note: says that the river's name is heard, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: A man is spotted in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man, but it is the verb to guy, to mock. The Tees is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to poke fun at them, a synonym of tease.

clue.text: The people voting having to get up

definitions.meaning: the number of electors who come to the polls
to rise from bed or appear dressed and ready, as in to be well turned out

explanation.surface: Voters complain that they must rise early to cast a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnout is the body of voters at an election, and to turn out is a phrasal verb for rising or getting up.

clue.text: I see man carelessly making a bloomer

indicators.note: words put down carelessly come out in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Someone spots a man blundering clumsily into an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carelessly' rearranges the letters of I SEE MAN. 'bloomer' looks like a blunder, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesia is a South African garden flower, so it is a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Liquid refreshment for an emperor

definitions.meaning: a hot drink of port or sherry with sugar and spice
the title of the ruler of Ethiopia

explanation.surface: A drink is brought to a visiting monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus is both a mulled wine drink named after Colonel Negus and the Amharic title of the Ethiopian sovereign.

clue.text: Clarify and edit a clue that's obscure

indicators.note: an obscure or muddled version of the words is their letters in a jumble

explanation.surface: A crossword editor is told to rewrite a puzzling clue so solvers can follow it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's obscure' rearranges EDIT A CLUE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To elucidate is to explain or make plain, a synonym of clarify.

clue.text: During class, a pupil relaxed

parts.note: in form, a form being a school class
L for learner, the plate on a pupil driver's car

explanation.surface: A schoolchild lounges about in the middle of a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: A FORM is a British school class; L is a learner, as on the L-plates of a pupil driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal means casual and easygoing, the same as relaxed.

clue.text: Side promises to be entertaining

parts.note: a facet is one side of a cut gem or of a question
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: One faction pledges to put on a good show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' only links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Facetious remarks are flippantly humorous, meant to amuse.

clue.text: Old man after silver

indicators.note: the man word is put after the silver word in the answer

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
Ed is a man's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: An elderly fellow goes in pursuit of a hoard of silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' signals the order. 'Old man' looks like one phrase, but 'Old' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged is a straight synonym of old, elderly.

clue.text: Unknown animal in ark, hors de combat

indicators.note: the letters fight and so are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A creature aboard Noah's vessel is out of action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combat' rearranges ARK and HORS DE; hors de combat is French for 'out of the fight', disabled.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark horse is a little-known competitor, literally an unfamiliar racehorse.

clue.text: 26 attending church, escorted by gentleman in a muffler

indicators.note: the gentleman surrounds the other pieces, as escorts flank someone

parts.note: Sir is a title of address for a gentleman

indicators.note: the 26 piece goes alongside the church piece

parts.note: the answer to 26 across, shortened to its familiar form Len
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A man goes to church with a gentleman, wrapped in a scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escorted by' and 'attending' signal the container and the charade; 26 is Leonard, familiarly Len. A muffler is not a scarf here but a device that quietens a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A silencer muffles the noise of a gun or engine, so it is a type of muffler.

clue.text: Cheerful young girl broadcasting

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young society woman
being on air means transmitting on radio or TV

explanation.surface: A happy young woman is presenting a radio show.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair means suave and light-hearted, carefree, so cheerful.

clue.text: Fine bridge player leads diamonds

indicators.note: the bridge player goes first, leading the diamonds word

parts.note: N is North, one of the four players at the bridge table
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: At the card table a good player opens with a diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads' places N before ICE. North, South, East and West are the bridge seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice and fine are interchangeable words for pleasant or satisfactory.

clue.text: Clergyman follows woman executive

indicators.note: the clergyman word follows the woman word in the answer

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A vicar takes over from a female manager at the top of the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' signals the order: the clergyman comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: A director is a senior executive on the board of a company.

clue.text: Lad's absorbed — brown study — that's natural

indicators.note: the lad has taken in the brown word, which goes inside

parts.note: a lad is a boy; the 's is 'has'
tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: A boy is lost in thought, which seems quite natural.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbed' signals the container. 'brown study' looks like the phrase for a reverie, but the two words do separate jobs here.
explanation.definitionFit: Botany is the science of plants, a branch of natural history.

clue.text: Show support — impede robbery

explanation.surface: Protesters display their backing but block a theft.
explanation.definitionFit: Hold up can mean exhibit, prop, or delay, and a hold-up is an armed stick-up.

clue.text: Talking down to coves, to converts

indicators.note: converts is a verb here, changing the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone addresses a group of fellows condescendingly while winning them over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converts' rearranges TO COVES TO. 'Talking down' suggests condescension but means speaking quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sotto voce is Italian for 'under the voice', speaking in a low tone, lowering one's voice.

clue.text: A slim woman, mum, holding work up

indicators.note: the mum word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: sh is a call for silence, as is mum

indicators.note: in a down clue the work word is read upwards

parts.note: to ply is to work at a trade

explanation.surface: A thin woman and her mother are carrying some work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the work word round (YLP) and 'holding' signals the container. 'mum' looks like a mother but means keep quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sylph is a graceful, slender girl or woman.

clue.text: It is old, with no speed at all

parts.note: nought miles per hour, written 0 mph

explanation.surface: Something is antique and does not move at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' here is sex appeal or vigour, a sense the capital disguises.
explanation.definitionFit: 'It' in the sense of sex appeal or zest is the same quality as oomph, vigour and allure.

clue.text: Bicycle was blue

definitions.meaning: a pedal cycle with a small motor

explanation.surface: Someone's bicycle was painted blue.
explanation.definitionFit: A moped is a low-powered motorbike, and moped is the past tense of mope, to be dejected.

clue.text: Age concealed by fat man

indicators.note: the age word is hidden away inside the fat word

parts.note: lard is pig fat
an eon is an age or very long period

explanation.surface: A man's years are disguised by his bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed by' signals the container. 'fat man' suggests one phrase, but 'man' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonard is a man's first name, so it is a fair example of a man.

clue.text: Show approval of a striker

definitions.meaning: one who shows approval by applauding
the tongue inside a bell that strikes it

explanation.surface: A crowd applauds a goalscorer.
explanation.walkthrough: The striker is not a footballer but the part of a bell that hits it.
explanation.definitionFit: A clapper is someone applauding, and also the metal tongue that strikes the inside of a bell.

clue.text: Big, strong dog

definitions.meaning: a sledge dog of the Arctic

explanation.surface: A large powerful hound is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Husky means burly and brawny, and a husky is an Arctic sled-dog breed.

clue.text: Bird with split crest

parts.note: to part is to split or separate
a ridge is a crest, as of a hill

explanation.surface: A bird whose head plumes are divided is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crest' suggests feathers, but it is the top of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a game bird of the pheasant family.
